_doc: OPS-MONITORING-INVENTORY-HOST-SYNC-W1 Ch3 — config for monitoring-inventory-reconcile.py's SOT_PARITY check. That check answers the one question the rest of the reconciler cannot: is the DECLARATION this instance reads still the one that is committed? Every other check reads the inventory and assumes it is true; this one audits that assumption. Missing or unparseable => the check reports COULD_NOT_COMPARE, never a pass — an unreadable config means the audit did not happen, which is not the same as agreement.
_why_the_inventory_only: Ch2's declaration-sync.sh flows four .json declarations, but this check deliberately covers ONLY monitoring-inventory.json. Listing the other three here would duplicate a set that already has an owner (the DECLARATIONS array in declaration-sync.sh), and a duplicated fact drifts — the exact class this whole arc keeps retiring. The inventory is also the only one of the four whose staleness silently corrupts every other check's premise.
_enforcement_semantics: report = SOT_PARITY findings are logged with positive per-host output and are EXCLUDED from the drift set, so they never page and never set `drifted`. block = findings join the drift keys and feed the breach streak. Ships as `report` on purpose: a sync that is merely a few minutes behind a just-merged commit is not an incident, and a check that pages on transient lag gets muted or deleted within a week — the severity-ladder discipline this repo learned from the session-drift detector.
_promotion_criterion: report -> block only after 30 consecutive daily runs, on BOTH hosts, reporting IN_SYNC with ZERO COULD_NOT_COMPARE — counted by the operator from the reconciler's own CHECK SOT_PARITY lines, a number that can be checked rather than a vibe. The COULD_NOT_COMPARE half is the load-bearing half: it measures whether raw.githubusercontent.com is reliable enough from these boxes to be a blocking dependency, which is the actual open question about this transport. Flip is owned by OPS-MONITORING-SOT-PARITY-PROMOTE-W{NEXT}; do not flip it here.
_measured_propagation_delay: raw.githubusercontent.com serves this path with `cache-control: max-age=300` (measured 2026-08-05, with a live `x-cache: HIT` on a pre-push body 30s after the merge landed). So a host's worst-case lag behind a merge is ~5 min of CDN TTL PLUS up to the 60-min sync interval, not the interval alone — and a SOT_PARITY run inside that window reads DRIFTED while nothing is wrong. This is the concrete reason the check ships `report`: the first unattended aoe-1 fire after this wave's own merge correctly returned UNCHANGED because the CDN was still serving the old body. The daily reconciler runs at 06:57/07:17, far from any normal merge, so a DRIFTED reading there is unlikely — but 'unlikely' is exactly what a promotion criterion is for measuring rather than assuming.
_why_not_compare_to_the_deployed_checkou: signal-1 has /opt/crypto-quant-signal-mcp at origin/main, which looks like a cheaper local SoT. It is not usable: aoe-1 has no git checkout at all (measured — /opt holds only algovault, algovault-monitoring, containerd), and the checkout itself only advances on a deploy, which `paths-ignore: ops/monitoring/**` prevents for exactly the commits this check exists to catch. Comparing against it would make the check structurally blind to its own subject.
